players.product: High-speed data cables for AI / HPC data centers (capabilities up to 1.6 Tb/s)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jon Boaden on FY2026: revenue grew 14.4% to $1.243 billion (organic 14.2%); underlying operating profit grew almost 20% to $127.3 million at a 10.2% underlying operating margin (from 9.8%); underlying basic EPS $0.435 (+20%); underlying EBITDA $164 million (+22%); return on capital employed 21%. By end market: Complex Industrial Technology +56.3% organic to $382.9 million; Off-Highway +20% to $279.3 million; Consumer Electricals -7.8% to $242.4 million; EV and Electrification +4.8% to $181.8 million; Medical -10.5% to $156.2 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $1.243 billion (+14.4%, organic 14.2%); underlying operating margin 10.2%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Boaden: data center revenue doubled year-over-year as AI infrastructure investment drove demand for Volex's high-speed cables; Volex deployed incremental capacity and held additional critical components to support customers, and demand for data center products was sustained at similar levels in the first quarter of FY2027. Outside data centers, Complex Industrial Technology grew approximately 12% organically across industrial and defense customers. Volex's two biggest customers are one in data centers and one in electric vehicles; no other customer is greater than 4% of revenues.
quarterly_data.figure: outside the two biggest customers none above 4% of revenues; ~12% organic growth outside data centers

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nat Rothschild: Volex has 'an extraordinary opportunity in data centers over the next five years, and quite possibly even longer'; hyperscalers are a very concentrated industry and working so closely with one does not exclude working with others in the future; Volex built the data center business from nothing over the last 15 years. CFO Boaden: Volex also supplies power products into data centers, and as data-center power evolves to DC at 400 and 800 volts - the same voltage and DC currents as its EV business - its EV engineering and vertical integration apply to data-center power products.

Outlook: trading to date in FY2027 is strong and in line with expectations; CEO Rothschild said Volex is conservatively forecasting 5% growth on the Complex Industrial Technology side; continued strong demand expected from industrial and defense customers in FY2027; Medical demand expected to stabilize in FY2027 and move into growth over the medium term. Path to the $2 billion medium-term target (CEO): around $500 million of organic growth (share gains with existing customers, moving up the complexity curve, North America white space) plus around $300 million from acquisitions, with 200 basis points of margin expansion to a 12% underlying operating margin, roughly doubling underlying operating profit to around $240 million; CFO: 10% margin is now the baseline, not the ceiling.
quarterly_data.figure: Complex Industrial Technology forecast 5% growth; ~$500 million organic + ~$300 million acquisitions to $2 billion; 12% margin; operating profit ~$240 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Boaden: EV and Electrification growth was supported by a full-year contribution from a major vertically integrated charging program for a European charging infrastructure business; Volex is diversifying into energy storage (connecting batteries to solar generation, using EV-like DC voltages and connectors), where CEO Rothschild says cables, connectors and plastics are all made in-house; first-quarter EV demand has been strong as consumers adopt EVs in response to higher fuel costs. When tariffs shifted, Volex relocated EV cable production without disruption to quality or lead times.

CFO Boaden on other end markets: Off-Highway growth came from a significant European defense vehicle program with potential for follow-on orders, the ramp of North American programs (building on the European position acquired with Murat Ticaret) with initial customer wins, and growth in India plus a commercial-vehicle upturn. Consumer Electricals declined on intensified Chinese competition in Europe as Chinese appliance makers redirected exports away from the US because of tariffs; Volex secured new domestic appliance harness programs, a harness selling for five to 10 times the power cord. Medical declined on anticipated customer destocking, with new program wins in advanced treatment, imaging and diagnostics.

CFO Boaden on cash and costs: capital expenditure typically runs at 3%-4% of revenue, with most projects approved on a payback within two years; working capital rose, principally inventory, to support data center revenue growth and customer relocation initiatives, bringing cash conversion to 63.9% (over 90% before capex) and underlying free cash flow to $42 million; Volex exercised a one-off option to purchase previously leased freehold land and buildings in Turkey. Inflation pressure, mostly from Turkey, was largely offset by efficiency savings and customer pass-through; higher freight costs (oil, Middle East conflict) are passed through to customers, and production in Turkey continues unaffected.
quarterly_data.figure: capex typically 3%-4% of revenue; cash conversion 63.9%; underlying free cash flow $42 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Rothschild: Volex operates 23 sites across Asia, Europe and North America with 13,000 colleagues, and 14 of its top 20 customers are leaders in their field. It has not done an acquisition for almost 3 years after looking at probably 50 companies, as valuations have increased slightly; criteria include a post-acquisition return on capital of at least 15% within two years and around 15% operating margins, and it has 'a number of extremely interesting opportunities'. Volex supplied a PCBA used on the recent NASA Artemis mission, and the CEO sees humanoid robots (Tesla's and competitors') as an opportunity Volex wants to try to work on.
quarterly_data.figure: 23 sites; 14 of top 20 customers category leaders
